messages.subject: Help with acoustic analyses
messages.body_plain:
Dear All,

I'm currently working on a project dealing with underwater noise. I'm interested in determining the relative difference in noise level between 3 different areas that I sampled.
More specifically I would like to focus on the 100-700 Hz frequency range to obtain:
- the average intensity of the noise (within the specified frequency range) for each area;
- the average intensity of the noise for each frequency category (e.g. 0-100Hz, 100-200Hz...) for each area;
- the number of 'peaks' above a certain db value for specific frequency ranges for each area.

My samples consist in a series of 1-hour long .wav files collected in the 3 different areas during 2 sampling seasons.
The final goal is to show that Area1>Area2>Area3 in terms of noise levels. I'm not interested in absolute values as I had no possibility to use calibrated equipment. I'm only interested in the relative difference between the 3 areas.

I downloaded R packages TuneR, SeeWave and Ineq but I'm experiencing some hard time with R code.
I don't expect you to write the code for me but if you can point me toward some simple guide (I'm not an acoustician) that a newbie can easily follow, I would be extremely grateful.

Thanks for your time.

Best,

Sergio

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Help with acoustic analyses
messages.body_plain:
Hi Sergio,

Luis Villanueva-Rivera has put together a valuable primer of acoustic
analysis using R and other tools. It's here:

http://research.coquipr.com/pdf/Villanueva-Rivera.etal.2011.pdf

The supplemental materials include a tutorial with exercises:

http://1159sequoia05.fnr.purdue.edu/primer/Primer_Tutorial.pdf

best wishes,
jesse
